utterance:
Samuel, I've examined you and I'm quite concerned about what's going on. Here's what I found: your temperature is up a little (37.9), your pulse is fast (102), and when I pressed on your tummy the pain was very clearly in the right lower side, exactly where the appendix sits. The way your pain started around the belly button and moved to the right lower side overnight, plus you feeling sick, off your food, and hot and shivery, is the classic story for appendicitis — inflammation of your appendix. Your urine test doesn't show an infection, which supports this.

What I'm concerned about: an inflamed appendix can sometimes burst, and you already have signs that the lining of your tummy is becoming irritated. This needs to be dealt with today, not watched and waited on.

Here's my plan: I'm sending you straight to the emergency department of the hospital, and I'll phone them ahead so they know you're coming. There, a surgical team will examine you, likely do blood tests and a scan, and if it is appendicitis, the usual treatment is an operation to remove the appendix — often keyhole surgery. The sooner it's done, the safer it is.

Important: from now on, please don't eat anything solid, and don't eat anything at all until the hospital team sees you. A few sips of water are okay, and I'll give you some paracetamol now to take the edge off the pain on the way. Please don't drive yourself — get someone to drive you or take a taxi, and go now, not later.

Safety netting — things to watch for on the way: if the pain suddenly becomes much worse or spreads across your whole tummy, if you start vomiting repeatedly, if you feel faint or sweaty, or if you spike a high fever, call 000 immediately — that could mean the appendix is bursting. Don't take anti-inflammatory drugs like ibuprofen or aspirin in the meantime. If for any reason you don't make it to the hospital, or the pain changes dramatically, call an ambulance or come straight back here — but the expectation is that you'll be seen today in ED. Do you have someone who can drive you?
reply: Yeah, I'll be okay. I'll get someone to drive me. My mate's coming.

awards.label: Phone the emergency department with a handover
Refer to the emergency department today for surgical assessment

utterance: Alright Samuel, I've spoken to the emergency department and they're expecting you, so you should be seen quickly when you arrive. Here's your summary card, and I'll keep the details on file. To recap: this looks like appendicitis, and my notes, your exam findings, and the urine test are going with you so the hospital team has the full picture. Remember: nothing solid to eat from now, sips of water only until they say otherwise, you've had paracetamol so avoid other painkillers — especially ibuprofen or aspirin — and go straight there now with your mate. If anything worsens on the way — sudden severe pain, pain spreading across the tummy, repeated vomiting, faintness or a high fever — call 000 straight away. Take care, and I hope the surgery goes smoothly.
